solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Young rascal, one stealing fish

parts.note: to whip is British slang for to steal, so a whipper is a thief
the snapper is a family of food fish

explanation.surface: A cheeky youngster is caught pinching fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip' is informal British for steal, a sense many solvers outside Britain will not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an impertinent young person, usually a cheeky boy, is called by this old-fashioned word.

clue.text: Use milk that's off? Not grand for this

definitions.text: Use milk that's off? Not grand for this

indicators.note: milk that is off has gone bad, so the letters of the phrase use milk are spoilt into a new order
not tells us to leave out the letter for grand from the mixture

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, and a grand is a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A breakfast tip: if the milk has turned, don't waste it on something grand.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffling USE MILK gives seven letters; 'Not grand' removes the K to leave six. The whole clue doubles as the definition: a cereal you pour milk on.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes a breakfast cereal of oats, nuts and fruit, eaten with milk.

clue.text: Removal of line during one edit, possibly

indicators.note: the line comes during, i.e. in the middle of, the rearranged letters
possibly signals that the letters of one edit may be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: An editor cuts a line in a single pass over the text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ONE EDIT, and 'during' puts L inside that mixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: striking something out of a text is its removal.

clue.text: Thoughtlessly spouted normal nonsense, if has broken leg

parts.note: par is the normal or expected standard, as in feeling below par
rot is a British word for nonsense

indicators.note: broken says the letters of if has are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: the leg side in cricket is also called the on side

explanation.surface: Someone babbles absurdly after a fall that broke their leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges IF HAS into FASHI. In cricket the leg side is also called the on side, so 'leg' gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: words repeated like a parrot's mimicry are said mechanically, without understanding.

clue.text: Following one's bloke up mountainous area

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom upward

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
one is I, and one's is read as one is, giving I and S
Sam stands in for any ordinary man's name

explanation.surface: A man climbs into the hills after a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is taken as 'one is', giving IS. As this is a down clue, 'up' reverses F, IS and SAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Geological term: a compact group of mountains forming a distinct block is called this.

clue.text: Unrestrained shoot that spreads rapidly

parts.note: wild means unrestrained or out of control
to shoot a gun is to fire it

explanation.surface: A plant puts out a vigorous shoot that grows like a weed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoot' looks like a plant's growth but is the verb fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: news spreads like a raging blaze in dry country, hence anything that spreads rapidly.

clue.text: Provided home security for one away in Southsea, perhaps

definitions.text: Provided home security for one away

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of the town might be read in another order

explanation.surface: Someone watched over an absent friend's place in a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: SOUTHSEA, a seaside district of Portsmouth on England's south coast, contains exactly the right letters; 'perhaps' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone who lives in an absent owner's dwelling to guard it has done this job.

clue.text: Competed around a run that's changed

indicators.note: around tells us the word for competed wraps round the other letters

parts.note: vied means competed
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Racers contended around a course whose route had been altered.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something altered or made different has been changed.

clue.text: Game birds, swimming in pairs

definitions.meaning: a pastime of skimming flat stones across water
male and female mallards paddling together as couples

explanation.surface: Game birds swim on the pond two by two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game birds' reads as one phrase but splits: 'Game' is the stone-skimming pastime, and the birds are the females and males of a duck species.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal and figurative: the stone-skipping pastime is named after the waterfowl couples, females alongside males.

clue.text: False rumours have inlays poorly fitted in Tenerife and the like

indicators.note: have means hold within, so the false rumours contain the other letters

parts.note: canards are false reports or hoaxes

indicators.note: poorly fitted inlays are out of place, so their letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Gossip about bad dental or tile work on a holiday island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly fitted' rearranges the inlays, and 'have' means the false rumours hold that mixture. 'Tenerife' tempts as a single island, but the plural 'the like' asks for the group.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Tenerife is one of a Spanish archipelago off north-west Africa, and the rest are its siblings.

clue.text: Old man's regularly seen in old hat

parts.note: pa is an old word for father, the old man, so old man's gives pa plus s

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter of seen

explanation.surface: Father is often spotted in a dated hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: out of fashion, no longer current, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Lyrically romantic harp playing before disco dances

indicators.note: before puts the first group of letters ahead of the second
playing has the letters of harp performing in a new arrangement
dances sends the letters of disco whirling into another order

explanation.surface: A harp performance precedes a disco night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' turns HARP into RHAP; 'dances' turns DISCO into SODIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: effusively emotional, like an ecstatic musical composition.

clue.text: Favouring upper class priest and model first

parts.note: Eli was the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible
the Model T was Ford's famous car
first is written 1st, read as IST

explanation.surface: A snob prefers the toffs: the vicar and the model come first.
explanation.walkthrough: ELI is the Old Testament priest; the Model T Ford gives T; 1ST, with the one read as I, gives IST.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who believes a privileged minority should lead holds this view.

clue.text: A couple of fellows feeling size initially matters

parts.note: F abbreviates fellow, so two of them give FF
an air is a feeling or impression, as in an air of mystery

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of size

explanation.surface: Two men reflect that size, at first, is what counts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' looks as if it modifies 'matters' but signals the first letter of 'size'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: business concerns or things to be dealt with, as in the state of public business.

clue.text: Short time before Ray moved to new school years ago

indicators.note: before puts the short time ahead of the rest

parts.note: a second is a short moment, as in wait a second

indicators.note: moved shifts the letters of Ray into a different order

parts.note: modern means new

explanation.surface: Ray changed to a new school just before term began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' rearranges RAY to ARY. This was a type of British state school for pupils who failed the eleven-plus exam, largely phased out in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a former British state school category for pupils not selected for grammar school.

clue.text: Church put up note about a Christian involved in fashion sections of the Observer

indicators.note: put up, in a down clue, sends the following letters upward, reading them backwards
about says the note surrounds the designer

parts.note: so, also soh, is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
Christian Dior was the French fashion designer

explanation.surface: A church posts a notice about a fashionable Christian, a story in a Sunday newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the note round the designer, giving SDIORO, which 'put up' reverses in this down clue. The Observer is a British Sunday paper, but here it means anyone looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomy: these are vascular layers of the eye, and an observer is someone who uses their eyes.

clue.text: Having undergone chemical change made man moan?

definitions.meaning: combined with oxygen, as rust forms on iron
turning the word man into moan works by adding O, the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Something unpleasant happened to make a man complain.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: adding O, the symbol for oxygen, to MAN gives MOAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry: a substance that has combined with oxygen, like rusted iron, has undergone this reaction.

clue.text: Get rid of a limitless role held by out-of-work clergyman

indicators.note: held by says the trimmed role sits inside the trimmed clergyman
op, short for opus, is a work, so out-of-work removes those letters

parts.note: a bishop is a senior clergyman

indicators.note: limitless means losing the outer letters at both ends

parts.note: taken as written, before trimming

explanation.surface: An unemployed vicar takes on a part with no restrictions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out-of-work' drops OP (opus, Latin for a work), leaving BISH; 'limitless' loses the outer letters; 'held by' puts the trimmed role inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to formally put an end to a law or practice is to get rid of it.

clue.text: A Rodin sculpture excursion? Quite the opposite

definitions.note: an ex- trip outward reversed becomes an in- movement into territory, a noun

indicators.note: sculpture suggests the letters are shaped anew, as clay or marble would be

explanation.surface: A trip to see a Rodin statue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sculpture' rearranges A RODIN. The definition swaps the ex- of excursion for its opposite: an incursion.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposite: an excursion goes out, whereas an advance into enemy territory is an incursion.

clue.text: Child wearing small hat as crash helmet

indicators.note: wearing joins the child to the hat that goes with it

parts.note: S abbreviates small, as on clothing labels
a kid is a child
lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A little kid in a tiny hat pretends it is a motorcycle helmet.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: bikers call protective headgear for motorcycling by this informal name.

clue.text: Story about a big-chested northern boy

indicators.note: about means the lie wraps round the rest

parts.note: a story can be a lie, a tall tale
DD is a large bra cup size

explanation.surface: A tale about a buxom woman told of a lad from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' has the story wrap round the rest; 'big-chested' points to a large bra cup size.
explanation.definitionFit: Regional usage: Scots and northern English speakers call a young lad by this word.

clue.text: Extremely pussy ear — oh, or awfully pussy gums

indicators.note: extremely means taking the extreme letters, first and last, of pussy
awfully says the letters of ear oh or are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A disgusting medical complaint about a pus-filled ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' takes P and Y from 'pussy'; 'awfully' rearranges EAR OH OR into ORRHOEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical: this is periodontitis, inflammation of the tooth sockets with discharge of pus.

clue.text: I clearly said home help's back

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: back says the help is read in reverse

parts.note: aid is help, and help's is read as help is

explanation.surface: Someone states plainly that the domestic helper has returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I clearly said' is the code word radio operators use to spell out the letter I. 'back' reverses the help, read with 'help's' as 'help is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alphabet code: in the NATO phonetic alphabet, used to say letters unambiguously, the letter I is spoken this way.

clue.text: Once again call girl is in Brazilian capital

indicators.note: is in says the girl sits inside the money

parts.note: the real is Brazil's currency, capital in the sense of money
Di is a short girl's name, for Diana

explanation.surface: A call girl is working in Brasília.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests Brasília, but it means money: the real is Brazil's currency. 'Once again call' also hides the call girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Telephone usage: to dial a number a second time is to call it once more.

clue.text: Side uppermost in Nashville? Gee whiz, just the first side playing

indicators.note: playing has the letters performing in a new order
just the first means only the first letter of whiz is used

explanation.surface: A country singer in Nashville is amazed that only the record's A-side is played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just the first' keeps W from 'whiz'; 'playing' rearranges GEE, W and SIDE. Nashville signals the American spelling; British usage prefers edgeways.
explanation.definitionFit: American usage: with the narrow edge foremost or upward is the US form of edgeways.
